DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia, first episode, active phase.

The patient is a 26-year-old male with a 3-month history of prodromal symptoms (withdrawal, depression) followed by 6 weeks of active psychosis characterized by persecutory delusions (NSA surveillance/control), bizarre behavior, and functional impairment. His work-up for medical, metabolic, substance-induced, and mood-associated causes is negative. The clinical picture is consistent with a primary psychotic disorder, specifically schizophrenia.
